newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine slum violence enters third day.
newsitem.headline: Philippine slum violence enters third day.

text.p: Philippine police opened fire and used tear gas on Wednesday after pitched battles in central Manila with hundreds of slum dwellers armed with petrol bombs, broken bottles and darts, witnesses said.
It was the third straight day of clashes between police and residents of a slum colony in the city's Binondo district.

The squatters were trying to prevent government wrecking crews from demolishing more than 500 shanties and semi-concrete houses they had built on private property. Many of them have been living in the area for more than a decade.
At least six people were injured, including a 14-year-old boy struck by a bullet, while 13 squatters were arrested, police and hospital staff said.
Witnesses said demolition began after police cleared the area of militant squatters.
About 3.5 million people live in squatter colonies in and around Manila, representing 39 percent of the capital's population, the National Housing Authority says.
The government has launched a campaign to demolish the "blighted areas" to develop them into commercial zones.
The Binondo residents set up a barricade of logs and steel bars on a street leading to their homes but the wreckers set it on fire after spraying it with petrol, witnesses said.
As police and demolition crews advanced, residents standing on the roofs of their houses hurled rocks, darts, broken bottles and petrol bombs, witnesses said.
Police on balconies of nearby buildings fired tear gas to disperse the squatters.

"I have lived here since I was 14 years old. Now I am a mother of three," a sobbing housewife said as government teams ripped down her house. "We won't leave this place even if we have to live on the streets."
Many slum dwellers have defied eviction orders, saying government proposed resettlement areas are overcrowded, filthy and far away from their jobs.
